schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: The device that HOLDS aider in-process so it can do build typing on CC's behalf. It is a Cairn device — its own process, its own charter, instance 0 — that imports a foreign program (aider, a git checkout at ~/dev/src/aider, v0.86.3.dev HEAD 5dc9490bb) and drives it through its Python API. Three things make it a device rather than a wrapper. FIRST, THE INTERCEPTOR: aider reaches every model it will ever reach through exactly one call site, `res = litellm.completion(**kwargs)` in Model.send_completion (measured 2026-08-16 by grep over the whole tree — one chat-completion call site, every coder and every edit format and every retry path funnelling through it). the interception point is `sys.modules['litellm']` — a surface module installed there BEFORE aider is imported, so the real litellm is never imported at all. It answers the eight callables aider touches (completion, completion_cost, model_cost, get_model_info, validate_environment, token_counter, encode, transcription — the last on the voice path only, and it refuses) plus the 23 exception classes aider's `EXCEPTIONS` list names, and translates completion into `inference_domain.domain.resolve`. THE SLOT WAS THE CHART'S ANSWER AND IT WAS MEASURED WRONG DURING THE BUILD: survey held that replacing aider's lazy `LazyLiteLLM` slot before first attribute access would suffice, because it had grepped `litellm\.` — which finds attribute ACCESS and is structurally blind to `import` statements. `aider/exceptions.py` does a bare `import litellm` at lines 68 and 87, and `simple_send_with_retries` constructs `LiteLLMExceptions()` on EVERY call, so the real module would have loaded on the hot path with the slot dutifully replaced. Pre-empting `sys.modules` covers both roads and is the smaller change — `LazyLiteLLM` keeps working untouched, since its `importlib.import_module` of that name now returns ours. SECOND, THE FENCE: the same object refuses by model name and provider at the seam, so the ask cannot widen — and because the injection point and the fence are one object, they cannot drift out of agreement with each other. THIRD, THE TRANSLATION: its input is a cast ticket's berthed chart chain plus ONE decompose piece — survey holdings become the file list, constrain bounds plus the piece become the prompt, the ticket's proofs become aider's test loop — and its output enters proven-space through the UNCHANGED physics: proofs twice, tester seal, verdict artifact, clearance gate. It has no HTTP face, no route, no port, no server (one web server), and it never runs aider as a subprocess (a subprocess imports nothing and would slip the sieve while breaching the law the sieve enforces). AND THE REPO MAP IS OFF, WHICH IS PART OF THE TRANSLATION AND NOT A PERFORMANCE SETTING. aider's `map_tokens` walks the whole repository and splices a ranked digest of it into the prompt — content assembled by the HELD PROGRAM, after translate.py has finished counting spans. So falsifier clause (7) could be violated while the instrument that watches clause (7) reported zero untraceable spans, because the violation happens downstream of the only thing that can see it. `Brief.map_tokens = 0` closes it at the one place it can be closed, with a tooth that reds if it moves. It is also Law 1 twice over: the chart chain already settled which files a piece touches (survey's holdings, constrain's bounds), so a repo map is aider re-deriving the settled by heuristic. MEASURED, NOT REASONED — the first live fire died in `repomap.get_ranked_tags` on `import networkx`, a module this device's own venv closure had correctly measured as lazy-only and therefore never installed; the traceback is what surfaced the prompt hole, and installing networkx would have hidden it. FOURTH, SINCE 2026-08-17, THE DRIVER — and it is what turned this device from a description of an offload into one. `driver.drive_brief` takes a Brief, runs the real aider Coder inside the shim's venv interpreter, and comes back as SERIALIZABLE DATA: the files as they stood before, the files as they stand after, what aider reported it edited, how many asks the fence allowed, and any error, appended to ~/.cairn/devices/aider_shim/0/drives.jsonl. The interpreter boundary is why the result is data and never a live Coder — the loop is in-process with aider and out-of-process from CC at the same time — and the seam across it is a SPEC STRING rather than a callable: a "module:attr" or "/abs/file.py:attr" resolved inside the venv, because a callable cannot be JSON. That string is also the only window in which the environment can be arranged BEFORE `aider.models` is imported, which is what made the network scar below findable at all. `driver.survival` is the reader that answers, per file, whether the drive's edit is still what the drive left. FIFTH, SINCE 2026-08-18, THE PIECE'S TEST RUNS TWICE ON EVERY DRIVE, AND THE TWO RUNS ARE NOT INTERCHANGEABLE — this is the one sentence a reader of this device most needs and the one nothing else in it says. THE FIRST RUN IS AIDER'S: the Coder is constructed `auto_test=True, test_cmd=<the brief's string>`, so after edits land aider runs the command itself, and a failure sets `self.reflected_message`, which is the SOLE thing that makes `run_one`'s `while message:` loop ask again (base_coder.py:1616-1622 — `auto_test` is the only gate on that block). Its output is FEEDBACK TO THE APPRENTICE and is evidence about nothing else; nothing records it. THE SECOND RUN IS THE PARENT'S: `driver.run_test`, further down the same module, unchanged, out-of-process from aider and after it — and it alone is THE RECORD'S AUTHORITY. `DriveResult.test` is that run, always, and every probe, verdict and ticket that speaks about whether a driven piece passed is reading it. Until this date the ctor line read `auto_test=False` with the comment 'WE run the test, so its result is ours to carry' — true about the record, and silently also deciding that a failing test never reached the model at all, so `num_reflections: 0` read identically for 'converged on the first try' and 'nothing could ever have reached it'. That second consequence was nobody's decision. `test_cmd` rides the venv boundary as a STRING and can be nothing else, MEASURED not chosen: `commands.cmd_test` accepts a callable, but `get_platform_info` does `platform_text += self.test_cmd` unguarded (base_coder.py:1169) on every system-prompt format, so a function raises TypeError before the first ask. `max_reflections` still defaults to 0, so the loop is opt-in per drive and the cap is the caller's — the change made the feedback REACHABLE, it did not make it automatic. THE COST IS REAL AND IS NOT YET MEASURED: every failing drive now runs the piece's tests twice and may buy a second ask against a metered host, which is exactly what the third probe below watches.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM: every line of code in this system is typed by the most expensive model available, including the lines whose shape was already settled three chart stages earlier. A decompose piece that says what to build, a constrain bound that says what is out, and a proof that says when it is right together describe the work closely enough that the typing is transcription — and transcription is what a 30B coder model on a box we already own is for. The offload is not about cost alone; it is about WHERE the expensive resolver is spent (Law 1: on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled). THE OTHER HALF OF THE WHY IS THAT THIS IS AN EXPERIMENT AND IT IS ALLOWED TO FAIL. The claim under test is that a cheaper model, handed a chart chain, can produce work that passes the same gates unchanged. If it cannot, the honest outcome is a red measured against a baseline, not a relaxed gate — which is exactly why constrain put 'relaxing, bypassing or special-casing any gate the output must pass' out of bounds. The unchanged physics IS the experiment. And it rehearses the thing that comes after: this is the first component whose OUTPUT is judged rather than whose behaviour is, which is the shape the cocoon needs.
invoke: import: `from cairn.devices.aider_shim import shim` (the fenced surface) or `from cairn.devices.aider_shim import driver` (the builder loop: `drive_brief(brief)` -> a DriveResult, recorded; `drives(path)` and `survival(rec)` read it back). Prove: `cairn test cairn/devices/aider_shim` for all six, or one at a time — `python3 cairn/devices/aider_shim/proofs/test_driver.py` (exit 0 = green) — or under the tester with `cairn test --netns --seal <path>`, which is the only hand that may mint a validation. The proofs need no network by construction — every model call in a proof goes to a fixture; the only real dial is the live fire, which is not a proof.
entry: FRESH design; the foreign program is HELD, not grafted. aider's bytes stay at ~/dev/src/aider, unmodified — modifying it is out of bounds, because a change we make there is unversioned by us and makes the measurement unrepeatable. What is borrowed is an idea and it is cited rather than copied: aider's own LazyLiteLLM is the pattern that makes the interception clean, and it was written for startup speed, not for us. The seam it accidentally provides is the entire reason this device is small.
state_and_history: compiled to state.json (projected window) + history.json (append-only voyage) beside this charter — the charter-state-history split; this file stays pure intention+why. Runtime state — which pieces were driven, what came back, what it cost — is instance-space at ~/.cairn/devices/aider_shim/0/ and never here.
filed_edges: (a) THE SIEVE IS BLIND HERE AND THE CHARTER SAYS SO RATHER THAN INHERITING A COMFORT. cairn/tools/import_sieve builds its graph over OUR repo's .py files and computes which of OUR modules reach a target. A third-party client imported by a HELD FOREIGN PROGRAM is not in that graph — so the sieve would not have caught aider dialing out, and a green sieve is not evidence about this device's sole-path compliance. The evidence is the fence proof and `interceptor.installed()` — an IDENTITY check (is the module at that name OURS?), not the absence check the chart wrote. The chart's criterion said `'litellm' not in sys.modules` after a driven run, and that instrument would have gone red at the moment the design succeeded, since the whole mechanism is to PUT something there. The distinction is carried to the verdict rather than edited into the berth. This is a second residue beside the subprocess one inference_domain's charter already names, and it is owed a ticket.

(b) TELEMETRY LOADS IN OUR PROCESS. posthog and mixpanel are required at aider's import time via aider/analytics.py (measured 2026-08-16 by AST closure over `from aider.coders import Coder`). Whether they can transmit, and whether a held foreign program with telemetry clients loaded in-process is acceptable as a standing arrangement, is a question NO LAW IN THE CORPUS CURRENTLY ADDRESSES — the sole-path law is about the inference host specifically. It is an escalation to Akien, not a thing to configure around quietly.

(c) ONE PIECE PER INVOCATION IS A DECISION, NOT A DISCOVERY. The ambiguity — whole ticket or one decompose piece — was carried openly from orient through constrain and settled at decompose on three grounds: a piece already carries its own what/why/kind so the prompt has a stated aim without one being invented; triage already produces the order, so a whole-ticket shim would re-derive a sequencing the chain has settled (Law 1's defect); and concentrating a multi-piece build loop here would put complexity in one component, which degrades every tier of Claude (ruled 2026-08-16). It grows into the larger against a measured need, if one appears.

(e) THE REFUSAL'S SHAPE IS CONSTRAINED BY A HANDLER NOBODY KNEW TO WRITE DOWN. The design worried about one absorption path — aider retries its `exceptions_tuple()` with backoff to RETRY_TIMEOUT, so a refusal wearing a litellm error name would burn 60s on a decision that will never change. Parsing aider's actual handlers found a second and worse one sitting beside it: `except AttributeError: return None` in `simple_send_with_retries`, which would turn a refusal into 'the model returned nothing' — silently, with no record and no red. That is falsifier clause (4) reached by a road the charter's prose did not name. The tooth for it is DERIVED, not transcribed: the fence proof parses that function's except-handlers each run and requires AskWidened to be caught by none of them, so it survives aider changing its handlers under us. Recorded here because the lesson generalises past this device — a claim of the form 'X propagates out of foreign code untouched' is a claim ABOUT that code, and the honest instrument reads the code rather than listing what we remember it catching.

(d) THE BASELINE THE FALSIFIER NEEDS DOES NOT EXIST. The ticket compares the shim's CC tool-call count against a direct build's, and nothing counts the calls today — it is a hand's act, as the 2026-08-14 ruling says plainly. The probe carries the shimmed half; the baseline half is owed.

(f) THE PROBE'S MEASURED COLUMN WAS READ OUT OF A KEY THE VERDICT DOOR HAS NEVER WRITTEN, and this edge is filed because the FIX is local while the SHAPE is not. The probe read `artifact['criteria']` and compared outcomes to `'passed'`; the door writes `artifact['verdicts']` with OUTCOMES `('pass','fail')`. Every real artifact therefore yielded zero rows counted and `passed: False` — the measured half of this device's watch structurally dead, reporting green=0 forever underneath a carrier that looked healthy. Seventeen sealed teeth stood over it and none bit, because the proof's FIXTURE hand-wrote the reader's invented shape: a fixture that agrees with the READER instead of with the WRITER proves only that one head agrees with itself, and that is a class of hollow proof the tester cannot detect. Closed here by composing the door (OUTCOMES imported, `verdict_error` asked, one tooth building its artifact THROUGH `write_verdict`), and mutation-validated 3/3. WHAT IS NOT CLOSED: nothing in the corpus reds a proof whose fixture was never checked against the producer it stands for — the survey-floor trouble standing in the inbox today is the same shape at a different seam. Owed a ticket, and it is not this device's to own.

(g) THE DEFAULT ASK-LOG WROTE NOWHERE, AND 24 GREEN TEETH COULD NOT HAVE SAID SO. `drive_brief(log_path=None)` built a SeenLog with `record_path=None` — an in-memory log that died with the venv process — so every ask the fence allowed was recorded correctly and then lost. A FIXTURE THAT SUPPLIES AN ARGUMENT CAN NEVER FALSIFY THE DEFAULT THAT SUPPLIES NONE: every tooth passed a tmp path, so the default was the one arrangement no fixture exercised. The first live fire found it, which is the only thing that could have. Closed by importing the fence's own DEFAULT_RECORD rather than re-spelling the path — two spellings of one path is how a store quietly becomes two — with a tooth that asserts the identity and a mutant that reds when the resolution is removed.

(h) MODEL CONSTRUCTION DIALS THE NETWORK WHEN THE CACHE IS COLD, AND THE FIRST MEASUREMENT SAID OTHERWISE BECAUSE THE CACHE WAS 19 HOURS OLD. aider's ModelInfoManager falls through to a bare `requests.get` against raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm whenever its 24h JSON cache misses — a road the interceptor does not cover, because it is not a litellm call at all. The tooth that 'proved' no network re-staged the model seeding inside its own in-venv script, so it measured the arrangement and not the driver: mutating the driver's real seed line left it green. Closed with a seam that sets HOME to an empty directory (a guaranteed cold cache) and replaces `requests.get` with a recording tripwire, then drives the REAL `drive_brief`. The mutant now reds naming the litellm URL. This is a THIRD residue beside (a): the sieve is blind here for the same reason — a third-party client imported by a held foreign program is not in our import graph.

(i) THE APPRENTICE DID NOT PRODUCE AN EDIT — CAUSE FOUND, REPAIRED, AND THE EDGE KEPT BECAUSE THE READING THAT MISATTRIBUTED IT IS THE LESSON. Two live fires against qwen3-coder:30b on hex returned prose and a fabricated filename instead of a SEARCH/REPLACE against the files it was handed: `aider_reported_edited: []`, no file hash moved, 1 allowed ask, 0 reflections. Every layer above read that as the model being weak at the pinned 'diff' format. IT WAS NOT THE MODEL. The brief's prompt is 13,932 chars, but the PAYLOAD aider builds from it was 289,601 — its system prompt, 129,319 chars of read-only reference and 141,238 chars of editable files — and hex reported `prompt_eval_count: 4271`. ollama's `num_ctx` defaults to 4096 whatever the model's own context_length says, and an over-long ask is CLAMPED silently: HTTP 200, a fluent answer, no field saying anything was dropped. The apprentice was answering an instruction with none of its files attached and SAID SO in the reply we filed as evidence of weakness ("since no files have been added to the chat yet, I'll create the new file") — the record contained its own refutation and was read past. Re-asking the captured payload at num_ctx 81920 processed 65,164 tokens and returned a well-formed SEARCH/REPLACE naming the right file. THE REPAIR is three numbers becoming one (`Fence.ask_ctx`, below) plus a clamp check that reds the answer instead of applying it. THE EDGE STAYS OPEN on the half that is not fixed: nothing about the pinned edit_format, the one-ask cap, or the brief's size was actually tested by those fires, so the questions they raised are still unanswered rather than answered no — and 45% of that payload was aider's own source, carried as read-only reference the piece did not need. What the brief hands the apprentice is a bounds question for Akien (Law 9), not a fix to make unilaterally.

(j) THE ASK'S SIZE IS ONE NUMBER NOW, AND IT IS STILL A HAND'S NUMBER. `Fence.ask_ctx` is the single source for all three quantities that have to agree — what aider is told it may send (`get_model_info`/`model_cost`, minus `reply_headroom`), what the host is asked to allocate (`options.num_ctx` on the resolve request), and the ceiling the answer is measured against (`check_processed`). Before 2026-08-17 they lived in three places and disagreed by 20x without anybody deciding they should. THE CLAMP CHECK HAS NO ESTIMATE IN IT, deliberately: comparing the host's count against ours would need a tolerance, because this device's `token_counter` is chars//4, and a tolerance is where a real truncation hides. A clamp fills the window to the brim; a fit leaves headroom. AND THE INSTRUMENT WAS ALREADY ARRIVING: `provenance.counters` has carried `prompt_eval_count` through `domain.resolve` since inference_domain was built, and this device was already unpacking it into aider's `usage` object without ever asking what the number meant. A free measurement, unread, for the device's whole life. WHAT IS STILL OWED: 81920 is measured on ONE box at n=1 (hex, a 32 GB M1 Studio: the captured payload loads at 26.9 GB and answers; 98304 returns empty after 11s). The method is written down at the field, so the number is re-derivable rather than folklore — but a hand-set constant in a gate is a learned value stranded in a human's head, and a second provider on the fence would need its own reading with nothing to take it.

(k) AN ASK THAT FAILED IS STILL AN ASK, AND THE RECORD DENIED IT — SO THE DEVICE LIED ABOUT WHERE THE SILENCE CAME FROM. On 2026-08-17 a live fire returned in 29s with no edits, no error and ZERO rows in the ask log, and the driver reported in good faith that the drive had REACHED NO MODEL. It had. The ask went to hex, hex answered, and the answer carried no token counters at all (the response keys were `['created_at','done','message','model']`); `inference_domain.host.metered_cost` refuses rather than metering zero, so `HostUnmetered` was raised AT OUR SEAM — and every `log.record` in `interceptor.completion` sat AFTER the door returned, so a raising door wrote nothing. A false statement in a record of truth, produced by an honest reading of an incomplete one: Law 7, and the breach is in the RECORD, not in the reading. THE REPAIR IS ORDER, NOT CLASSIFICATION: the door call is wrapped and the row is written BEFORE the raise, with a fourth verdict `failed` carrying the exception's type and message verbatim. The driver then reads `verdict == 'allowed'` rather than a row count — only an ALLOWED ask means the apprentice was heard from, and an empty edit list is evidence about the model only when one exists. Two unheard shapes now say so in the drive record and raise `DriveRefused`: no ask at all (setup — with the two measurements that would tell which, files-on-disk and files-inside-the-driven-repo) and asks-but-none-allowed (the fence's own dispositions ride the message verbatim).
AND THIS FALSIFIED A CLAIM THIS DEVICE HAD ASSERTED IN PROSE SINCE ITS FIRST BUILD. `fence.py` said `AskWidened` "propagates out of aider untouched", and the design had genuinely gone looking — it found `LiteLLMExceptions.exceptions_tuple()` (23 classes) and deliberately stayed outside it so the refusal would escape the 60s retry loop. It escapes THAT loop. It does not escape aider: `base_coder.py:1506` catches bare `Exception`, prints the traceback to aider's OWN io, calls `self.event('message_send_exception')` and RETURNS. Derived from the installed source 2026-08-17, the handler list on the `send_message` call path is `['KeyboardInterrupt', 'litellm_ex.exceptions_tuple()', 'KeyboardInterrupt', 'FinishReasonLength', 'Exception']`. One absorber was looked for and found; the broad one two lines of control flow later was never looked for at all. SO: A REFUSAL CANNOT BE MADE LOUD BY CHOOSING A CLASS NAME. It is made loud by writing the record at the seam, where nothing downstream can swallow it — Law 7 is satisfied by the record, never by the exception's flight path. The proof does not assert that aider still swallows: a tooth that reddened the day aider FIXED this would be good news read as a defect, so the tooth drives a stand-in handler of the same shape and PRINTS aider's real list as a measurement beside it. STILL OWED, and it is the falsifier's middle arm: no drive has yet carried a piece brief -> APPLIED EDIT -> test result. The blocker is now sized, not mysterious — hex answered at 289,601 chars / `prompt_eval_count` 65,164 and returned no counters at 299,167 chars, where aider's own count was 74,791 against a `max_input_tokens` of 73,728. `ask_ctx: 81920` is therefore at or past this box's edge at n=1, and 45% of that payload is aider's own source carried as read-only reference the piece does not need. Both are bounds questions for Akien (Law 9), not a widening this device may take on its own.

(l) THE BRIEF HANDED AIDER THE WHOLE SURVEY, SO EVERY PIECE OF EVERY SPLIT GOT THE SAME FILE LIST — AND IT WAS OVER THE WINDOW. `translate._files` read the survey berth's holdings and made all of them editable, so the eight pieces of the decompose split produced eight BYTE-IDENTICAL file lists weighing ~74,090 tokens against `Fence().send_budget()` = 73,728. The piece's own `uses` — a berthed field the decompose gate refuses to leave unresolvable, naming exactly the holdings that piece composes — reached the prompt as PROSE and was ignored at the one hop where it decides something. That is Law 1 at the last hop: a question the chain had already answered, re-derived (or rather, not derived at all) by the translator. NOW `brief()` selects from `uses`, and the measured span across the same split is 6,798–41,873 tokens, every piece under budget. THE SAFETY CHECK WAS A CENSUS, NOT A JUDGEMENT: across 51 berthed decompose packets, 321 pieces, exactly ONE carries no `uses` (235 of 236 build pieces carry it; 85 of 85 compose). So the no-`uses` case is real and rare, and the disposition is to REFUSE with the count in the message — falling back to the whole survey is precisely the behaviour being removed, and the fix for the one is upstream in the split. The shorter list is not a quiet drop: every holding is still in the prompt under THESE ALREADY EXIST, so the apprentice can still SEE what it may not EDIT.

(m) AIDER'S ROOT WAS UNPINNED, AND UNTIL THE FILE LIST SHRANK THAT WAS A COINCIDENCE NOBODY HAD SPENT. With `use_git=False` aider has no repo to ask, so `Coder.__init__` sets `self.root = utils.find_common_root(self.abs_fnames)` (base_coder.py:476, read by AST — there is NO `root` constructor argument, so this is not a bound we forgot to pass, it is a derivation we did not know was happening). While edge (l)'s whole-survey list spanned `cairn/`, that common ancestor WAS the repo. The first drive with a piece-scoped list had ONE editable file; the ancestor collapsed to `cairn/devices/aider_shim/`; and the apprentice's `cairn/devices/aider_shim/driver.py` landed at `cairn/devices/aider_shim/cairn/devices/aider_shim/driver.py` — a new file, nested, while the file it was asked to edit was never touched. THE FIX IS ONE ASSIGNMENT AFTER CONSTRUCTION, because construction is what computes the wrong one. AND THE SECOND HALF IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS MORE: the drive record imaged `b.files` on BOTH sides, so a write outside the brief left every imaged hash equal and `hashes_moved` reported nothing moved while a file was created. The only trace of the misplacement anywhere in the system was aider's own `aider_edited_files`. A record of truth that cannot witness an out-of-bounds write cannot report one (Law 7), so the after-image now covers aider's reported paths too, and a path we never imaged enters `before` as `{"exists": false}` — the true statement about a file that did not exist when the drive started, and NOT an image taken now, which would record the drive's own output as the state before it and make `survival` read a created file as `untouched`. Pinning the root makes the case rare; it does not make it impossible, which is why the record's eyes are the durable half and the pin is the convenience. Both are teeth (`test_aiders_root_is_the_REPO_not_the_ancestor_of_the_file_list`, `test_the_record_WITNESSES_an_edit_the_brief_never_named`), and the fixture that makes them bite puts the editable file one directory DOWN — with a single file at the repo top the ancestor happens to BE the repo and the defect is invisible. Both mutants died; killing the pin reproduces `pkg/stray.py` exactly.

(n) THE MIDDLE ARM LANDED, AND THE FIRST LIVE DRIVE FALSIFIED THE TOOTH SEALED FOUR HOURS EARLIER. 2026-08-17, piece 0 of aider-builds-a-piece: one ALLOWED ask (hex, 37,729 chars, prompt_eval_count 9,389, cache miss), `aider_reported_edited` and `hashes_moved` agreeing, and a test that RAN — brief -> applied edit -> test result, the falsifier's middle arm, complete for the first time. The test came back returncode 1, and that is a RESULT rather than a failure of the arm: the apprentice answered a brief whose only editable file was `venv.py` by emitting a whole new module body for `driver.py` with an empty SEARCH block, which aider appended, putting `from __future__` at line 480. The arm is about the chain being complete; whether the apprentice is any good is the NEXT measurement, and it now has an instrument.
AND THE RECORD CAUGHT ITS OWN AUTHOR. Edge (m)'s new eyes worked — the stray `driver.py` was witnessed, exactly as designed — and in the same act the record LIED about it: the before-state was written `{"exists": false}`, and `driver.py` had existed all along. Teaching a record to see out-of-bounds writes and to misdescribe them is one defect, not two, and it is the same one the edge is about: stating what was not measured (Law 7). `{"exists": false}` was TRUE FOR THE FIXTURE — a created file — and false in the world, which is the fixture agreeing with the reader instead of the writer, caught by live fire rather than by a tooth. THE HONEST ANSWER IS A SENTINEL, `{"unimaged": true}`, and it is a sentinel rather than a late image because a before-image not taken before is not a before-image. `survival` gains a FIFTH answer, `unknown_before`: it can still say `survived` (does the world hold what the drive left? — decidable) and must refuse `reverted` (was it what it used to be? — not decidable). A smaller answer on purpose, where the alternative was a confident one that is sometimes false. Second tooth, on the shape live fire actually took — a stray edit to a file that EXISTS — and the mutant that restores `{"exists": false}` kills both teeth.

(o) THE HOST ANSWERS 200 WITH A GO ZERO-VALUE AND WE READ IT AS 'NO COUNTERS'. Chased as an intermittent flake across four drives and finally cornered 2026-08-17 by capturing the exact /api/chat payload and replaying it with curl: hex returns HTTP 200, 96 bytes, in 0.1s — `{"model":"","created_at":"0001-01-01T00:00:00Z","message":{"role":"","content":""},"done":false}`. That is Go's zero-valued `api.ChatResponse`: no `error` key, no `done_reason`, no counters, `done` FALSE. ollama collected nothing from the runner and reported it as success. THE HYPOTHESES IT KILLED, each by measurement: not the payload (the identical bytes returned pec=9,359 / done_reason=stop three times in a row twenty minutes later), not `num_ctx`, not ask size, not the cache (the tee proved the call reached `host._post`, so it was never a hit), and not the message list (one message failed while the wedge held and succeeded after it cleared). WHAT IT IS: host-side, transient, and it wedges — while wedged, every request returns instantly; once cleared, everything passes. OUR SEAM ALREADY SURVIVES IT correctly — `metered_cost` refuses rather than metering zero, and since edge (k) the row is written before the raise, so the drive record names it verbatim instead of claiming the model was never reached. WHAT IS OWED IS THE NAME: `HostUnmetered` says 'no token counters', which is true and under-diagnostic. An empty answer at 200 is a DIFFERENT thing from an answer we cannot price, and the shape is now measured and cheap to detect (`done` false, no `done_reason`, empty content). That refusal belongs in `inference_domain`'s `_post`, which is another component's address — a ticket, not a reach across the fence.
gates: proof gate — proofs/ beside this charter, run by the tester under isolation='netns', run twice, with netns and non-netns outcomes required identical (a proof that passes only outside the netns is reaching the host, and its seal would be a statement about hex's availability rather than about this code). Durability gate: not done until proven AND committed. Money gate: the fence proof, which must red on a widened ask AND must fail if its seen-names log is empty — a green earned because nothing was asked is the hollow green this device is most exposed to.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) the module at sys.modules['litellm'] after a driven run is not ours — `interceptor.installed()` is False — so the interception did not hold and the sole path is a policy rather than a construction; (2) a model call reaches a provider without passing this device's completion — the fence was bypassed rather than refused, which is the money failure; (3) a widened ask (weak_model or editor_model naming a different model) is served rather than refused; (4) a refusal is absorbed by any handler on aider's own call path — retried to RETRY_TIMEOUT by its exceptions tuple, swallowed by its `except AttributeError: return None`, or smoothed into a generic failure in what this device records (Law 7 at a record of truth); (5) inference_domain acquires a row, field, flag or branch for this consumer — the provider learned about its consumer, which is the ruling of 2026-08-16 and the reason domains exist at all; (6) a proof here passes without the netns and fails with it; (7) a prompt handed to aider contains anything not traceable to a berthed packet field — the chain stopped being the input and the conversation started being it. (8) THE EDITABLE LIST IS BUILT FROM WHAT A PIECE READS RATHER THAN WHERE IT WRITES. `translate._files` sources aider's editable `fnames` from the piece's `writes_to` ALONE and its `read_only_fnames` from `uses`, and the two are a strict partition. `uses` cannot stand in: it names survey HOLDINGS — things the sweep FOUND — so a build piece's output address is excluded from it by construction, and handing the apprentice the file it READS is the measured n=1 that bore ticket a-piece-names-where-its-output-lands (declared venv.py, edited driver.py, a sibling in the same folder, appended onto a live module). EQUALLY RED: a `writes_to` address that does not exist yet reported as `skipped` instead of passing through as editable — a build piece's target is a file aider must CREATE, so requiring existence would reproduce that exact defect at the exact function that fixes it. And a berth carrying no `writes_to` must REFUSE loudly, naming the stale berth and `/chart <ticket>`; a fallback here would put the guess back.
how_it_learns: THROUGH ITS PROBE, AND THE PROBE IS THE POINT OF THE DEVICE RATHER THAN AN OBLIGATION ON IT. This device exists to answer a question it cannot answer by running: can a Q4_K_M 30B coder, handed a chart chain, produce work that passes the unchanged physics? Every ticket built through the shim reaches a verdict artifact, and that deposit is the event — no poll. The probe at probes/offload_yield_probe.py carries, per shimmed piece: did it pass the unchanged physics, what did it cost in CC tool calls against the direct-build baseline, and whether CC had to supply context beyond the piece and the bounds (which is what would falsify the one-piece-per-invocation decision in filed edge (c)). It deposits to the hypothesize tree, beside what killed or confirmed each expectation. THE PROBE CARRIES NO AUTHORITY: it deposits and pokes; re-opening a node whose intention did not work is the owner's act (Law 6). The consumer is Akien at triage — offload-more versus pull-back is his call. A SECOND PROBE SINCE 2026-08-17, AND THE PAIR IS THE POINT. probes/edit_survival_probe.py asks the question the offload probe cannot: a ticket can pass its physics green while every line the apprentice wrote was thrown away and rewritten by CC — the offload buying nothing while reporting success, which is a hollow green (Law 8). It reads the driver's own drive records against the working tree and dispositions each driven piece survived | rewritten | discarded | not-applied, deduped on the drive's own identity because `enough` is a count. It does NOT collapse a mixture (Law 7): a drive whose files disagree is reported `mixed`, per-file carried whole, and the carrier names the HEAD the comparison was actually taken against — the spec says 'at the PROVED commit' and this reads the working tree, so naming the drift beats a second implementation that would have to be kept honest against the first. Same nexus, same five-piece population, same consumer, no authority. AND ONE GATE OF THIS DEVICE DOES NOT YET LEARN, WHICH IS SAID HERE RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE NOTICED: `Fence.ask_ctx` — the context window the ask buys, and the ceiling a clamped answer is caught against — is a constant, measured on hex at n=1 by posting a captured payload at candidate windows and reading `prompt_eval_count` back. The method is recorded at the field, so it is a coarse measurement to sharpen rather than a folklore number; but nothing re-runs it, nothing notices when the host's usable ceiling moves, and a second provider added to the fence would inherit hex's reading with no warning. The evidence needed to learn it is already being collected — every row of asks.jsonl now carries ask_chars, num_ctx and prompt_eval_count together, which is the population an estimator would read. A THIRD PROBE SINCE 2026-08-18, AND IT WATCHES THE COST OF THE FIX THAT ARMED IT. probes/reflection_earns_its_ask.py asks what the EXTRA ASKS BUY: it reads the same drives.jsonl the other two read, splits reflected drives from the unreflected baseline in that one population, and reports each side's applied-and-passing rate WITHOUT grading it — whether the difference is worth the tokens is Akien's call at triage, and a probe that answered it would be exercising authority it does not have (Law 6). Three things in it are deliberate and are recorded here because each is a way the watch could have lied. (i) A CACHE HIT IS NOT A SECOND OPINION: `prompt_eval_count` is None when no call was made, and only an ask AFTER THE FIRST that actually reached the host counts toward the five — the first cut of that predicate asked whether the DRIVE had more live asks than cached ones, which a live first ask and a cached second one satisfies, and a tooth caught it before the seal. (ii) THE CARRIAGE CHECK IS ONE-SIDED ON PURPOSE: the fence records `ask_chars` and never the prompt — so 'did the second ask carry the test's failure text?' is not readable from this store at all, and the probe reports the necessary condition it CAN read (the second ask grew by at least the failure text's length) with the word `consistent`, never `carried`. The containment itself is measured at the fixture layer by proofs/test_driver.py::test_the_second_ask_carries_the_tests_own_failure, through a seam that transcribes what it was asked; live, it is an owed instrument and the carrier names it as a hole (Law 10 — 'we have not built the measurement yet' is an ordinary state). (iii) THE STOP-EARLY FALSIFIER OVER-FIRES ON PURPOSE: the spec's state is 'a reflected drive that ends WORSE than its first attempt left it', and the driver images the files once before and once after the WHOLE drive, so the state after attempt 1 was never taken and cannot be computed later. The probe reports the record-visible shoulder — `left-changed-and-failing` — which is a superset, and says so in the carrier. Over-firing costs a human a look; under-firing lets the loop go on manufacturing the harm it was armed to catch, and giving a copying apprentice more turns to copy is how that harm would arrive.
traces_to: Law 1 — the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled. A decompose piece plus its bounds plus its proof is a settled answer; typing it out with the most expensive model available is re-derivation, and this device is the structure that answer becomes.

Law 8 and its why — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass, BECAUSE a peer system requires trust where a hierarchy does not (Akien, 2026-08-16). This device's output is judged by exactly the gates CC's output is judged by; relaxing one to admit it would destroy the measurement, and a false green here would be leaned on by a peer.
Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. Whether the offload works is unmeasured, is labeled a hypothesis throughout this charter, and is answered by the probe rather than by this build.
Telos 1 — every call metered, because it rides the sole pipe like any other consumer and moves yield_report like any other consumer.
owner: CC owns this device's code and proofs and gates writes to them. Akien owns the intention and ruled the operating shape on 2026-08-15 (traffic through the inference proxy so we learn from it) and the consumer/provider split on 2026-08-16 ('the consumer asks for what it wants. period, end of story'), which is why this device composes and asks and the proxy knows nothing about it. He also owns the one thing this device cannot decide for itself: whether a runnable aider — 24 third-party packages including two telemetry clients — may be installed on his box.
gated_by_why: THE HANDS THIS INTENTION'S OWNER-GATE ADMITS — the machine-readable half of `owner` above, and the only half cairn.devices.cairn.machines.harbor_master.clearance.clear() reads. CC alone, because the code and its proofs are CC's to gate; Akien's ownership is of the intention and is exercised by ruling, not by a clearance stamp.
proof: proofs/test_interceptor.py (15 teeth) — the eight-callable surface is complete, every exception name is catchable, no stray `*Error` attribute would break aider's dir() walk, the fallback exception list is checked against aider's own by AST, usage is never fabricated on a cache hit, and `installed()` is asserted in BOTH directions (True for ours, False for a foreign module at that name — the negative half is what carries falsifier clause 1). The touched-attribute set is required NON-EMPTY before it is required to be a subset, so a pass cannot be earned by nothing happening. proofs/test_fence.py (10 teeth) — a widened model and a widened PROVIDER are each refused before the host is touched (the injected door is a tripwire that raises if reached), the refusal is recorded verbatim and on disk, an on-fence ask is still ALLOWED (a fence that refuses everything is a wall, not a fence), the fence is exact-match against five near-misses, and the refusal is required to escape every except-handler parsed live out of aider's `simple_send_with_retries`. proofs/test_translation.py — every substantive span of a produced prompt traces to a berthed packet field (owed with piece 5). ALL TEETH WERE MUTATION-TESTED before the seal: 12 mutants injecting real defects (fence opened, fence fired late, refusal unrecorded, refusal absorbed, provider check removed, usage fabricated, surface shortened, stray *Error added, touched-recording blinded, identity check reduced to presence, state moved to class-space, exception list drifted) — 12 killed, and the two that survived the first round are why the last two teeth exist. All under the tester, netns, twice. proofs/test_driver.py (25 teeth) — the drive runs the REAL Coder behind the fence with a fixture resolver, the result is serializable, the repo map stays at 0, the ask cap holds, an undirected drive lands in the fence's own store, and the DRIVER ITSELF (not a restaging of it) reaches no network with a guaranteed-cold model cache. proofs/test_edit_survival_probe.py (16 teeth) — armed at the berth the ticket names (resolved against the repo root, not the CWD: the bare run was green and the netns run was red, and the sibling probe's identical tooth had been passing for a reason that was luck), each of the four dispositions distinct, a mixture reported `mixed`, the vocabulary proved a translation of driver.survival's own source, one drive appended twice still one drive, and `enough` unlowered by drives that applied nothing. MUTATION-TESTED at the seal: four mutants — hollow drive (8 teeth red), ask cap removed (1), in-venv model seed removed (1, naming the litellm URL), default ask-log resolution removed (1). Six proofs, green twice bare and sealed under netns. proofs/test_driver.py grew to 36 teeth on 2026-08-18 (piece 7, the reflection loop): a failing test provokes a second ask, that ask carries the test's own failure marker, the cap still holds against a failing test, `max_reflections` still defaults to 0 for every entry point, the arrangement carries the BRIEF's test command rather than a hardcoded one, and a PASSING test provokes no reflection. Their fixture is a seam answering a SEQUENCE of replies and transcribing each request to a sidecar — on disk because the seam runs inside the venv subprocess and the tooth reading it does not; the reply counter beside it needs no such thing, because `_seam` exec's the seam file once per drive and the module state lives in the process that increments it. RED-FIRST PAID TWICE: run against the unchanged driver these teeth produced criterion 3's evidence, and they also caught a defect in themselves — the first fixture used a reply whose SEARCH block would not match, which provokes aider's own failed-edit reflection and measures a different mechanism entirely; it went green against the driver it was supposed to red on. The replacement applies cleanly and still fails the test. proofs/test_reflection_earns_its_ask.py (25 teeth) — armed at the berth the ticket names (asked through the gate's own `armed_error`), a cached second ask does not count as a second opinion, `consistent` is never the word `carried`, a passing reflected drive has no carriage question rather than a green one, the ended-worse alarm admits it over-fires and does NOT fire on an unreflected failing drive or on a drive that applied nothing, the falsifiers speak before `enough` is satisfied, a refused drive lands in neither rate, and the probe grades nothing. Seven proofs.
